caption: The van, the tools and the groceries all come out of one account. Anyone else running a business off their personal card?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R38 000
p/m
Living in Durban
slides.body:
Male, 39
Married, two kids
Job: Qualified electrician, my own small operation
Net salary: R38 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond
slides.body: We bought in 2021 when the rate was kinder. The repayment has moved twice since then.

slides.title: Van instalment
slides.body: The van is the business. If it stops, I stop. That is the whole risk in one line.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Family of four, one big shop and the top-ups
slides.body: Two growing boys. This number goes one direction only.

slides.title: Fuel & van running costs
slides.body: Some weeks I drive to Ballito and back for a job worth R1 400. I still take it.

slides.title: Takeaways & site lunches
slides.includes: Garage pies, Nandos on the way home, weekend delivery
slides.body: I told my wife it was maybe R600. It is R1 800. Buying lunch on site every day adds up quietly.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Tools & materials, medical aid, school fees & transport, utilities, business insurance, family support, funeral policy
slides.body: R13 250, and a good chunk of it is really the business paying itself out of my personal account.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R38 000. That is meant to be the business float and the emergency money at the same time. It cannot be both.

slides.title: I could not tell the business from the household
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The van and the tools came to R12 000 a month, sitting in the same account as the groceries.

No bank login needed.
